SignCredential has a signer but never compares it to a registrar, a dean or the university authority, so any wallet can supply either signature. BUG: SignCredential doesn't tie the credential to the university it passes (no has_one = university), and nothing stops the same wallet signing twice in both roles. The "multi-sig" is two flags anyone can set.

BUG: initialize_university stores the authority argument but seeds the PDA by the signer. If they differ, the account can never be used: issue_credential re-derives the PDA from the stored authority and fails ConstraintSeeds, as the script shows with X naming U. create_disclosure_proof takes any credential_key and never checks the credential exists or belongs to the signing student (code reading; the script only exercised a student's own credential).
Revocation needs the university authority (has_one), which the script confirms. Revoked credentials reject new signatures and verify as false.

functional_evidence: sign_as_registrar and sign_as_dean accept any signer, so the multi-sig credential can be forged by an outsider. The core trust path is broken.

The resolver commits the entries root, then after the entries deadline posts result: a keccak merkle payout root, result and kit hashes, the total and a SOL bond. Anyone can challenge during the challenge window; if none, settle returns the bond and makes the escrow Claimable. Each winner claims with leaf keccak(0 || keccak(escrow || claimant || total_le)) and a sorted-pair proof; a receipt PDA blocks double claims.
